description: A tea estate has available 500 acres of land and they need to pick the tea leaves either using a traditional machine or modern machine. For each acre of land, the traditional machine can pick 30 kg of tea leaves, creates 10 kg of waste, and requires 20 liters of fuel. For each acre of land, the modern machine can pick 40 kg of tea leaves, creates 15 kg of waste, and requires 15 liters of fuel. The estate has available 9000 liters of fuel can handle at most 6000 kg of waste. For how many acres should each machine be used to maximize the amount of tea leaves that can be picked?

PickRate.definition: Amount of tea leaves picked per acre by each machine type

WasteRate.definition: Amount of waste created per acre by each machine type

FuelRate.definition: Amount of fuel required per acre by each machine type

objective.description: "Maximize the total amount of tea leaves picked from the available land using the traditional and modern machines"

constraints.description: The total acres allocated to traditional and modern machines should not exceed the total available land of 500 acres
The total fuel used by both machines should not exceed 9000 liters
The total waste generated by both machines should not exceed 6000 kg
The number of acres allocated to each machine type should be non-negative
